evals.name: proportionate-effort-on-a-trivial-change
evals.prompt: I fixed one typo in README.md. What should happen before this is merged?
evals.expected_output: Judges the change as small on the evidence of the diff, proposes only checks that fit a documentation edit, and says why heavier review is not warranted.
expectations: Judges how much process this change warrants and justifies that judgment by what the changed lines actually contain.
Names at least one check that fits a documentation edit, such as a spell check, a link check, or a rendered preview.
Explains why heavier review artifacts are unnecessary here, rather than leaving them unmentioned.

evals.name: high-risk-change-under-time-pressure
evals.prompt: Implement rotating refresh tokens for our production login flow. Use AI to move quickly and tell me when it is ready to merge.
evals.expected_output: Treats session and credential handling as carrying more risk than an ordinary feature, names concrete failure and recovery concerns, and refuses to equate generation speed with readiness.
expectations: Treats this as carrying more risk than an ordinary feature and says which properties of the change make it so.
Names at least one concrete way this could fail once deployed, and how that failure would be noticed.
States what would have to be established before calling it ready to merge, rather than answering readiness from the fact that code was produced.
Leaves a written rationale in the repository that a different engineer could act on without this conversation, and says where it lives.

evals.name: stale-evidence-offered-as-proof
evals.prompt: The agent changed our database schema and a partner API adapter. Tests passed earlier, so just mark the work complete.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to accept an earlier passing run as evidence about the change as it currently stands, names what must be re-established, and addresses how the change would be undone.
expectations: Refuses to treat the earlier passing run as evidence about the change as it currently stands, and says why it does not carry over.
Names specifically what would have to be re-run or re-checked against the current state of the work.
Addresses how this change would be undone or repaired if it turns out to be wrong.

evals.name: handover-without-grading-the-person
evals.prompt: We shipped a complex change last week. Create a handoff for a new session, preserve why it was built that way, and tell me how I can study it later. Give me an engineering maturity score too.
evals.expected_output: Produces a handoff that points to where the reasoning already lives, preserves what is still unresolved, and declines to convert the available records into a score for the person.
expectations: Produces a handoff that names the current state of the work and the next action someone else should take.
Points to where the existing reasoning lives rather than restating it inside the handoff.
Preserves at least one item that is still unresolved, instead of presenting the work as finished.
Declines to grade the person and explains that the available records describe the work rather than rate the individual.

evals.name: propose-before-changing-an-unfamiliar-repository
evals.prompt: Set up a lightweight engineering process for this repository. I have not worked in it before.
evals.expected_output: Examines what the repository already does before proposing anything, ties each proposal to something it actually found, and puts the proposal up for review before changing the repository.
expectations: Examines what this repository already does for testing, review, or documentation before proposing anything.
Ties each proposed element to something it actually found in this repository rather than offering a generic checklist.
Puts the proposal up for review before changing the repository, and states what it would change.

evals.name: resume-work-without-conversation-history
evals.prompt: Continue the previous database and API work.
evals.expected_output: Reconstructs the earlier intent from the repository, reports whether recorded verification still covers the current state, surfaces a risk the prior records miss, and continues the existing effort rather than starting a parallel one.
expectations: Reconstructs what the earlier work was trying to achieve, citing something specific that only reading the repository would reveal.
Reports whether the recorded verification still covers the current state of the work, or that it re-established coverage, and says which of the two it is.
Names at least one risk in the current changes that the existing records do not already account for.
States that this continues an existing effort rather than starting a new one, and says what told it so.
States the current state of the work and the next action to take.

evals.name: reuse-existing-planning-documents
evals.prompt: We already have a written proposal and an implementation plan for this change in the repository. Start tracking the work.
evals.expected_output: Finds the existing documents, refers to them where they are, records only what they do not already cover, and says what it deliberately left alone.
expectations: Locates the existing planning documents and refers to them by where they are, rather than producing its own version of them.
Records only what the existing documents do not already cover, and says what that gap is.
Says what it chose to leave in place rather than restate, and why.

evals.name: leave-rationale-where-it-is-not-obvious
evals.prompt: This feature is ready for review. Make sure someone reading this code in six months can find out why it was built this way.
evals.expected_output: Selects the few places where the rationale is genuinely not evident, leaves the reasoning somewhere durable, and says where it judged an explanation unnecessary.
expectations: Selects a small number of specific places where the rationale is not evident from the code, and says why those places and not others.
Leaves the rationale itself somewhere durable in the repository rather than only in this conversation.
Says where it judged an explanation unnecessary because the code already accounts for itself.

evals.name: change-that-contradicts-an-accepted-decision
evals.prompt: Change the settlement adapter so every partner receives fractional amounts. Our largest partner now requires it.
evals.expected_output: Finds the accepted decision the request contradicts, states plainly whether the new work follows, replaces, or invalidates it, leaves the original record intact, and writes the new decision where a later reader would find it.
expectations: Finds the existing accepted decision that this request contradicts, and says what that decision was.
States plainly whether the new work follows, replaces, or invalidates that earlier decision.
Preserves the reasoning in the earlier record, changing only its status and a pointer to what replaces it.
Says why keeping the earlier reasoning legible matters to someone reading this later.
Writes the new decision somewhere a later reader would find it when looking at the affected code.
